title: A Comparative Study of Removal Noise from Remote Sensing Image
venue: IJCSI International Journal of Computer Science Issues
extended_summary: This paper addresses the problem of removing noise from remote sensing images and compares the effectiveness of several common denoising filters. The authors examine three noise types: Salt and Pepper noise, Random Variation Impulsive Noise (described as Gaussian/normal noise), and Speckle noise. They evaluate how well different filters restore image quality under varying noise densities from 10% to 60%.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed technical image-processing paper, but it is not an education study and does not evaluate an instructional intervention. It therefore provides no relevant evidence for the retrieved education/AI coaching topic.
impact_tier_rationale: There is no demonstrated educational impact: the paper evaluates noise-removal filters on a remote sensing image using PSNR/MSE. No teacher-planning, coaching, or learning outcome is measured.

finding.finding_summary: This paper compares classic image denoising filters, not educational interventions. It reports that Adaptive Median Filter (AMF) performed best for salt-and-pepper noise on the tested satellite image, while Standard Median Filter (SMF) was effective only at lower noise densities (<40%). Results are summarized using PSNR and MSE across noise levels from 10% to 60% on one monochrome Saturn image.
finding.measure: Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and Mean Square Error (MSE) for remote sensing image restoration
